prompt: Explain India's climate targets under the Paris Agreement.
hook: India's pledges have names and numbers.

card.oneLiner: India's updated NDC pledges to cut the emissions intensity of its economy, reach about half of its power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030, and achieve net zero by 2070.
keyPoints: One target is emissions intensity, not total emissions.
Another is non-fossil installed power capacity by 2030.
India has pledged net zero by 2070.
India pairs its targets with demands for finance and technology.

framework.name: India's Updated NDC
framework.gloss: Quantified 2030 targets on intensity and non-fossil capacity.

framework.name: Panchamrit pledges
framework.gloss: Five commitments including net zero by 2070.

whatYouCanDo: Learn the difference between emissions intensity and absolute emissions.
Follow official updates to India's NDC.
Track progress against the 2030 capacity target.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Targets and their baselines are updated periodically.

prompt: Explain India's National Action Plan on Climate Change and its missions.

card.oneLiner: India's National Action Plan on Climate Change coordinates sectoral missions such as solar, water, and sustainable agriculture.
keyPoints: The NAPCC was released in 2008.
It set up eight national missions across key sectors.
States run their own climate action plans.
Missions have been revised as policy has evolved.

framework.name: National Action Plan on Climate Change
framework.gloss: Eight national missions on climate-relevant sectors.

framework.name: MoEFCC
framework.gloss: The ministry leading national climate policy.

whatYouCanDo: Find your state's climate action plan.
See which national missions touch your sector or region.
Ask how missions are funded and reviewed.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Mission structure has changed over time.

sources.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

prompt: Explain the National Solar Mission and India's solar growth.
hook: Solar went from niche to mainstream fast.

card.oneLiner: The National Solar Mission set escalating solar capacity targets, and India's installed solar capacity has grown rapidly as tariffs have fallen.
keyPoints: The mission set phased capacity targets.
Solar tariffs have dropped sharply through auctions.
Growth spans utility-scale parks and rooftop systems.
India co-founded the International Solar Alliance.

framework.name: Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission
framework.gloss: Phased solar capacity targets and incentives.

framework.name: International Solar Alliance
framework.gloss: Platform for solar cooperation among member countries.

whatYouCanDo: Check rooftop solar subsidy schemes for homes.
Compare solar tariffs with other new generation.
Understand land and grid constraints behind the headline growth.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Capacity targets are revised from time to time.

sources.title: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

prompt: Explain India's carbon market and the law behind it.
hook: India is building its own carbon market.

card.oneLiner: India is setting up a compliance carbon market where large emitters trade obligations, alongside its existing energy-efficiency schemes.
keyPoints: The Energy Conservation Act was amended to enable carbon trading.
A Carbon Credit Trading Scheme creates a compliance mechanism.
It builds on earlier efficiency schemes such as PAT.
Design details on targets and sectors are being rolled out.

framework.name: Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022
framework.gloss: Legal basis for a domestic carbon market.

framework.name: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023
framework.gloss: Framework for obligated entities and credits.

whatYouCanDo: Follow notifications from the power and environment ministries.
Understand the difference between compliance and offset markets.
Watch how targets are set for covered sectors.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. The scheme is being implemented in phases.

sources.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

prompt: Explain Mission LiFE and how it frames individual climate action.

card.oneLiner: Mission LiFE promotes pro-planet individual and community choices, positioning lifestyle change as part of the response to climate change.
keyPoints: It was launched in 2022 as a national and global initiative.
It focuses on everyday behaviours and choices.
It is linked into India's climate communication and NDC narrative.
It is presented as complementing, not replacing, policy and technology.

framework.name: Mission LiFE
framework.gloss: A behaviour-change initiative around sustainable choices.

whatYouCanDo: Pick a few high-impact habits rather than many small ones.
Bring LiFE ideas into schools, offices and housing societies.
Recognise that individual action works best alongside systemic change.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Framing individual action is itself debated.
